summary: Russian drone and missile strikes continued across Ukraine overnight, targeting energy infrastructure and residential areas in multiple regions. Ukraine's recruitment policies are being adjusted amid ongoing mobilization, while diplomatic tensions persist over energy deals and international funding. The situation remains volatile with active cross-border attacks and infrastructure damage reported.
key_points: Russian forces launched coordinated drone and missile attacks across Ukraine overnight, hitting energy infrastructure and residential buildings in Kharkiv, Kyiv, and other regions. (Source: @mon1tor_ua/76678)

Ukraine's parliament is revising mobilization reservation rules, reducing deferments for defense and energy sectors from 100% to 85% and heat/water services from 75% to 60%. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/33905)
A recruitment center officer in Kharkiv pushed a 74-year-old woman, causing fractures, and fled without providing assistance or calling an ambulance. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/33912)

Ukraine's Ministry of Finance reports a $29.5 billion shortfall in international funding due to unmet obligations, with budget losses reaching 50 billion hryvnias over nine months. (Source: @UkraineNow/84613)

Ukraine is set to receive approximately €3 billion in additional EU military aid following discussions between Zelenskyy and European Commission President von der Leyen. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/33894)
Russian naval drones were detected moving from the Black Sea toward Odesa, while Ukrainian forces destroyed two Russian boats with personnel aboard. (Source: @kpszsu/85598)
Putin indicated willingness to halt strikes on Ukraine only on election day if Kyiv decides to hold votes, according to Kremlin spokesperson Peskov. (Source: @UkraineNow/84618)

A recruitment center officer in Kharkiv pushed a 74-year-old woman, causing fractures to her femoral neck and collarbone. The recruitment officers did not provide assistance or call an ambulance, but instead drove away immediately. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/33912)

Ukraine's Ministry of Finance reports a $29.5 billion shortfall in international funding due to unmet obligations, with budget losses reaching 50 billion hryvnias over nine months. The total shortfall may reach 70 billion hryvnias by end of 2026. (Source: @UkraineNow/84613)

Ukraine is set to receive approximately €3 billion in additional EU military aid following discussions between Zelenskyy and European Commission President von der Leyen. This comes as the country faces ongoing energy infrastructure attacks. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/33894)

During prolonged power outages, water will be supplied according to a schedule due to the need to transport fuel and the requirement to shut down generators, stated Aleksandr Shkin, director of the Ukrvodokanalekolohiya association. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/33902)
The Roshen confectionery plant in Vinnytsia, owned by former Ukrainian President Petr Poroshenko, has come under attack, according to ground reports. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/33913)

Putin indicated willingness to halt strikes on Ukraine only on election day if Kyiv decides to hold votes, according to Kremlin spokesperson Peskov. This conditional statement suggests potential tactical pauses tied to domestic political considerations. (Source: @UkraineNow/84618)

Russian naval drones were detected moving from the Black Sea toward Odesa, indicating ongoing maritime pressure along Ukraine's southern coast. (Source: @kpszsu/85598)

sections.threat_assessment: Russian aerial and maritime attacks continue to target critical infrastructure across Ukraine, with recent strikes on energy facilities and residential areas demonstrating persistent operational capability. The revision of Ukraine's mobilization reservation policies may strain domestic support but aims to bolster military readiness. Ongoing funding shortfalls and infrastructure damage compound Ukraine's operational challenges, while Russian conditional statements about election-day pauses suggest tactical flexibility rather than strategic de-escalation. Maritime threats in the Black Sea and Persian Gulf highlight broader energy security risks affecting global markets.
sections.regional_response: European Union officials are preparing to deliver additional military aid to Ukraine, with approximately €3 billion in funding expected imminently following high-level diplomatic discussions. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has defended American energy dealings with Russia, dismissing European criticism as hypocritical given continued European energy purchases. Meanwhile, international financial institutions face mounting pressure as Ukraine's debt obligations to the IMF and World Bank total nearly $138.9 billion through 2061, raising concerns about long-term economic stability. Regional actors are navigating complex energy dependencies while supporting Ukraine's defense efforts.
sections.intelligence_notes: Ukrainian intelligence coordination is expanding through a new 17-member Coordination Center under the Cabinet of Ministers, incorporating personnel from the SBU, GUR, Foreign Intelligence Service, and police to determine enterprise criticality for mobilization reservations. Ground reports indicate targeted attacks on politically significant infrastructure, including the Roshen confectionery plant owned by former President Poroshenko, suggesting potential psychological operations or symbolic targeting. Cross-border drone activity remains concentrated along northern and southern axes, with particular emphasis on approaches to Kyiv and Odesa. Energy infrastructure continues to be a primary target, with scheduled water supply disruptions during power outages indicating cascading effects on civilian services. Diplomatic communications reveal divergent interpretations of 'energy truces,' with Ukraine asserting continued Russian attacks contradict any formal agreements.
